name: Kemlock Server
description: Kemlock Server is a self-hosted password manager written in Rust and shipped as one static binary with a built-in web vault. It answers the Bitwarden API as Vaultwarden does, so the Kemlock, Amethystora Vault and Bitwarden apps connect to it.

notes.text: First-run setup works only over HTTPS or from localhost. Caddy serves https://<container-ip>:8443 with a certificate from its own local CA, so the browser warns once. For production put a real certificate or reverse proxy in front and set DOMAIN in /opt/kemlock-server/.env.

There is no admin token. On its first start the server logs a one-time setup code that the setup page asks for: journalctl -u kemlock-server | grep -i 'setup code' (Alpine: grep -i 'setup code' /var/log/kemlock-server.log). A restart before setup makes a new code.

If the container's IP address changes, update DOMAIN in /opt/kemlock-server/.env and the site address in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, then restart kemlock-server and caddy. A reserved or static address avoids this.
